topic.title: The badge swipe is the real KPI
topic.claim: Three mandatory office days have little to do with collaboration and a lot to do with managers who can't measure work, so they measure presence.
topic.moment: You commute ninety minutes to sit on Teams calls with people on the same floor.

turn.believed: Return to office is about culture and teamwork.
turn.actually: Swiping in is the easiest thing to count, and a counted thing feels like control.

topic.because: Judging output takes effort and judgment. A badge report lands on the HR dashboard by itself, and an empty floor looks bad to the people paying the lease.
topic.payoff: If the meeting could happen from home, the office day was for someone else's spreadsheet.
topic.behaviour: Companies track swipe-ins and link them to appraisals; employees come in, sit on calls, and leave after the minimum hours.
topic.mechanism: Presence is easier to measure than output, so presence becomes the metric.
topic.send_to: The colleague who also took a call in the office stairwell because every room was booked.
topic.why_now: More firms keep tightening office mandates and linking attendance to reviews.

score.why: Three office days mean managers count presence because output is hard to measure. It's a rant most readers have lived.

topic.villain: a presence-tracking system that substitutes swipe-ins for real performance measurement
